title: Batch + Quantization Capacity Playbook Q2 Forecast
content:
Purpose:
This working sheet captures capacity projections and tradeoffs between quantization levels and batching configurations across our multi-region GPU fleet. Goal is to produce a prioritized, measurable rollout plan for Q2 2026 that increases throughput and reduces unit cost while bounding customer-facing quality regressions.

High-level assumptions:
- Traffic mix: 65% short-chat (<=128 tokens), 25% medium (129-512), 10% long generation (>512).
- Baseline model: open-llama-70B variant used in hosted-api default route for evaluation tests.
- GPUs considered: A100-80GB (a100-80), H100-80GB (h100-80), T4-16GB (t4).
- Perf tooling: internal perf harness (perf-harness v2) measuring tokens/s and p95 latency for end-to-end requests.
- Quality metric: prompt-specific BLEU/ROUGE is noisy; we use relative logits-delta + human eval pass rate on 200-sample prompt set (eval-set-quant-q2).

Table 1 — Baseline measured throughput and quality (median across 10 runs):
GPU,Model,Precision,BatchSize,SeqLen,Tokens_per_sec,Median_latency_ms,Human_eval_pass_rate
a100-80,70B,fp16,1,128,1200,45,0.92
a100-80,70B,int8,1,128,1700,38,0.90
a100-80,70B,int4-quant,1,128,2350,33,0.84
h100-80,70B,fp16,1,128,1500,38,0.92
h100-80,70B,int8,1,128,2100,32,0.90
T4-16,70B,int8,1,128,600,92,0.89

Table 2 — Effect of batching (int8 on A100):
GPU,Model,Precision,BatchSize,SeqLen,Tokens_per_sec,Median_latency_ms,Quality_delta_vs_fp16
a100-80,70B,int8,1,128,1700,38,-0.02
a100-80,70B,int8,4,128,6200,110,-0.02
a100-80,70B,int8,8,128,11000,210,-0.03
a100-80,70B,int8,16,128,16000,420,-0.05

Key observations from microbenchmarks:
- Quantization (fp16 -> int8) yields ~35-45% throughput uplift at batch size 1 with negligible human-eval delta (~2 percentage points).
- Aggressive int4 reduces quality more noticeably (~6-8 percentage points) depending on prompt type; better for short, instruction-following prompts than for code or math prompts.
- Batching provides linear-ish throughput increases but latency degrades nonlinearly; p95 latency exceeds SLOs at batch sizes >8 for interactive routes.
- H100 gives 10-25% better tokens/s than A100 for same config; T4 is cost-effective for embedding-heavy low-cost routes but underperforms for large models.

Projected capacity model (Q2 growth scenarios):
- Baseline tokens/s demand today (global): 250k tokens/s.
- Expected demand growth by end of Q2 (conservative): +20% = 300k tokens/s; (aggressive): +50% = 375k tokens/s.
- Current committed fleet (usable tokens/s at fp16, batch=1): a100-80 pool = 120k tokens/s; h100-80 pool = 80k tokens/s; burst/spot (mixed) = 30k tokens/s. Total = 230k tokens/s.

Scenario analysis (target: serve 300k tokens/s while maintaining interactive p95 <= 250 ms for 90% routes):
Option A — Scale hardware: add +4 H100 nodes (expected +60k tokens/s at fp16), cost = high CAPEX/commit.
Option B — Software improvements: roll int8 for non-sensitive routes + increase batching for background/async routes. Projection: int8 conversion across 60% of traffic (mostly short/med) gives effective fleet capacity uplift of ~38% => 230k * 1.38 = 317k tokens/s.
Option C — Hybrid: int8 rollout to 40% + add +2 H100 = meets target with lower cost.

Quality gating and routing recommendations:
- Route classification: tag routes as interactive | background | experimental.
- Interactive: default fp16 or int8 with strict A/B; p95 SLO <= 250ms. Batch size cap = 8. Only int8 on A100/H100. No int4.
- Background: allow larger batching (<=16) and int4 where human-eval pass-rate loss <= 5% on the relevant eval-suite.
- Experimental: can run int4 and custom quant profiles behind feature flags with canary rollouts.

Rollout plan (60-day sprint cadence):
Week 1-2: perf-run of int8 across 5 canary routes (low-risk interactive + two background). Collect eval metrics + token-cost delta. (Owners: Marco)
Week 3-4: expand int8 to 25% traffic with weighted routing; enable telemetry for human-eval-sampling, logits-delta, and regression alerts. (Owners: Priya)
Week 5-6: enable batching policy per-route: background routes batch up to 16, interactive batch cap 8; measure p95 changes and adjust autoscaler node targets. (Owners: Jonas)
Week 7-8: evaluate int4 on background routes with heavy caching; run 1-week A/B with human evals and rollback thresholds set to -6% pass-rate. (Owners: Aisha)

Cost/benefit numbers (back-of-envelope):
- Current cost per 1M tokens (fp16) = $0.96 (weighted fleet).
- Projected cost per 1M tokens (int8 widespread, 60% traffic) = ~$0.66 (-31%).
- Capex for +4 H100 = ~$240k/month committed vs. marginal infra savings if software-only yields same throughput.

Capacity table (projected by region after software rollouts + modest scale):
Region,Current_tokens_s,After_int8_40pct,After_int8_60pct,+2h100_add,Recommended_action
us-west1,95k,131k,150k,170k,roll int8 40% + add 1 H100
eu-west1,70k,97k,110k,130k,roll int8 60% (no hardware change)
ap-southeast1,40k,56k,64k,70k,roll int8 40% + monitor latency

Monitoring and KPIs to surface in Redwood Console:
- Per-route tokens/s and cost/token broken down by precision (fp16/int8/int4).
- Human-eval-sampled pass-rate by route and quant config (daily).
- Logits-delta distribution and top-10 prompt regressions.
- Autoscaler triggers: queue-length, p95 latency, observed throughput per GPU (tokens/s).
- Canary health: traffic fraction, error-rate, quality delta, rollback flag.

Open questions / risks:
- Model-specific sensitivity: some model families degrade more with int8; need per-model evals (action: run eval-set-quant-q2 across our onboarded models).
- Telemetry gaps: we currently do not tag tokens by precision in all routes; infra change required. (Jira: INFR-4762).
- Cold-start KV cache behavior with batching + quantized kernels — observed warmup penalty for long-context sessions. Need experiment to measure end-to-end user-observed latency for seq>1024.

Immediate action items:
- [ ] Instrument tokens/precision tags in request traces (owner: Marco, due: 2026-03-19).
- [ ] Create canary routes and schedule perf-harness jobs (owner: Priya, due: 2026-03-22).
- [ ] Cost model update with int8 pricing assumptions for dedicated pools (owner: Aisha, due: 2026-03-26).
- [ ] Draft customer-facing note for enterprise customers about potential quality deltas and staged opt-ins (owner: Jonas, due: 2026-04-02).

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep int4 experiments isolated to background-only traffic; early human evals look notably worse on code/math prompts.
- Watch out for billing/attribution changes when mixing precisions — we must reflect this in billing pipeline.
- Consider a small feature in the console to show "precision tradeoff" per route with a slider for product owners.

Appendix — quick reference benchmarks (short):
- A100 int8 batch=4 (seq128): ~6.2k toks/s, p95 ~110ms, eval-pass 0.90
- A100 int4 batch=8 (seq128): ~11k toks/s, p95 ~210ms, eval-pass 0.84
- H100 int8 batch=4 (seq128): ~7.8k toks/s, p95 ~95ms, eval-pass 0.90

If there are no objections from the canary owners by 2026-03-16 we will kick the int8 canary run. Comments inline welcome — this is intentionally a working sheet, not final planning doc.

History/log: created by Aisha Patel 2026-02-20. Iterated with Marco and Priya during infra sync 2026-03-08. Updated after perf-harness run 2026-03-12.
